reason: r21 removes the r20 box cache. r20 (NRO 5617ee906b0756af39676a6a3bdc4a4bf3b5fb55d5b1d18fed29978d552635fb, run on Eden 2026-10-24, installed bytes matching, user report: gauge disappearing) inserted the mask a second time cleanly, and 206 of 206 sane probe lines read the clip rectangle at left == right (110 32 110 64, bar at 110,38,238,166) with flags 0x1: a zero-width scissor, the gauge hidden. insert::enter compared the box it was about to write with the box it had written and returned early when they matched; sharpness sat at 350/350 tier 4 for the session, so the authored pair, the position pair and the rectangle were written on the row's first enter call and skipped for the rest of it, while the game rewrote its derived rectangle between calls. r21 writes the five words on every enter, for the one mask the plugin owns. The run also settles the mask's liveness check: it never reported, because a mask freed with its row is no longer walked, so its enter handler stops running. That removes r18's 90 seconds of writes into freed memory, and it also means the re-arm has no signal for that case: the plugin sits out the rest of the session and the gauge draws as the game builds it. The insertion itself has completed twice (r18, r20): the 5-word object array through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator with instance+0xd8 and root+0xa0 published, the draw block resized through the root's vtable slot 0x58 with main+0xa49b28's arithmetic from the row+8 pair (3 objects, 16 sequences: 56 bytes = 7 records, grown to 72 = 9), the class factory main+0xa4b6cc, the native linkers, the marker at +0x50. Not approved for distribution; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.
runtime_test: NOT RUN: r21 writes the clip box on every enter of the mask, with no cache of the last box. r20 ran on Eden 2026-10-24 (installed bytes 5617ee906b0756af39676a6a3bdc4a4bf3b5fb55d5b1d18fed29978d552635fb): the insertion completed (mask 0x441ca6b0, 5-entry map, 9-record cache) and 206 of 206 probe lines read a zero-width box, the gauge missing; its box cache is the cause. r18 ran the same day with the same outcome. r17/r16/r15 ran clean; r14 ran once and failed as reported.

limitations: r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r21 has not been run. Two completed insertions (r18, r20) each hid the gauge with a zero-width clip box; whether a rectangle written on every enter call survives to the scissor has no runtime evidence, and a mask freed with its row leaves the plugin idle for the rest of the session (no writes, no re-arm), because the enter handler that carries both the write and the liveness check stops running
